# Third-party notices

## CC-CEDICT — `cedict.json`

`cedict.json` is generated from **CC-CEDICT**, the community Chinese-English
dictionary published by [MDBG][]. It is used as the fallback gloss layer: the
curated legal dictionary in `src/data/dictionary.js` is consulted first and
always wins.

- **Source:** https://www.mdbg.net/chinese/dictionary?page=cedict
- **Licence:** [Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0][cc-by-sa]
- **Copyright:** © MDBG and CC-CEDICT contributors
- **Obtained via:** the [`cedict`][npm] npm package (ISC-licensed packaging of
  CC-BY-SA-3.0 data)
- **Generated by:** `tools/build-cedict.mjs`

### What this means in practice

CC-BY-SA is a **share-alike** licence. `vendor/cedict.json` is a derivative of
CC-CEDICT and remains under CC-BY-SA-3.0 — attribution must travel with it, and
redistributing a modified version means redistributing it under the same terms.

This affects the data file only. It does not reach the application source,
which merely reads the file at runtime; the two are aggregated, not merged.
If you would rather the project carried no share-alike component at all, delete
`vendor/cedict.json` and `src/lib/translate.js`'s glossary loader — the app
degrades to composing glosses from the curated dictionary alone, which still
covers every candidate in testing, just less fluently.

### Transformations applied

`tools/build-cedict.mjs` filters and reshapes the upstream data:

- headwords restricted to 1–6 Han characters (simplified preferred)
- variants, cross-references and surname-only entries dropped
- classifier notes (`CL:條|条[tiao2]`), bracketed pinyin and
  traditional\|simplified pairs stripped from definitions
- at most two senses per entry, truncated to 90 characters
- numbered pinyin (`rong2 zi1`) converted to tone marks (`róng zī`)
